On 6 October 2023, the resident complained to the landlord about the condition of her garden following repair works. The landlord replied at stage 1 on 31 October 2023, saying the developer had offered to fill the trenched area and level the garden, but the resident had declined as she wanted it to be re-turfed. The resident escalated her complaint on 1 December 2023 as she was not happy with the landlord's response. On 29 December 2023, the landlord sent its stage 2 complaint response, apologising and offering £50 compensation for not replying to her correspondence, and £15 for not acknowledging her escalated complaint. claim_types: Landlord's handling of the resident's concerns about the condition of her garden
evidence: The shared ownership agreement stated that defects could be reported during the defect liability period ending on 15 December 2022, after which the resident was responsible for repairs.
The landlord's records and inspection evidence addressed drainage repairs and whether garden-condition issues had been raised before the defect liability period ended.
The resident's emails and complaint correspondence described the garden as uneven after the drainage repairs and sought re-turfing or compensation.
The landlord's complaint policy set timescales for acknowledging and responding to stage 1 and stage 2 complaints.
partial_case.facts: The resident had been a shared owner of the property since March 2022 and told the landlord she was unhappy with the garden's condition following repair works carried out in December 2022. The complaint concerned the landlord's handling of the resident's concerns about the condition of her garden and the landlord's complaint handling. Between June and August 2023, the resident contacted the landlord regarding the condition of her garden following repairs carried out by the property developer. On 6 October 2023, the resident complained to the landlord about the condition of her garden following repair works. On 31 October 2023, the landlord replied at stage 1 and said the developer had offered to fill the trenched area and level the garden, but the resident had declined because she wanted it re-turfed. The resident escalated her complaint on 1 December 2023, and the landlord sent its stage 2 response on 29 December 2023, apologising and offering £50 and £15 compensation for communication and acknowledgement issues. The resident referred her complaint to the Ombudsman because she remained dissatisfied with the landlord's handling of her complaint.

orders: Payment of £50 to the resident for distress and inconvenience caused by complaint handling failure

key_reasoning_quotes.text: The landlord was not responsible to carry out maintenance or to make good damage caused to the garden. Its offer to arrange for the property developer to level the garden and put things right was reasonable in the circumstances.

The landlord’s offer of £50 compensation for its lack of communication with the resident was also proportionate and consistent with an amount we would expect when considering our remedies guidance where there had been a failing by the landlord which caused inconvenience to the resident.

The landlord made an offer which satisfactorily resolved the failings it was responsible for. This leads to a determination of reasonable redress in its handling of the resident’s concerns about the condition of the garden.

In summary, the evidence shows there were delays in the landlord’s complaint handling process. Although the landlord offered some redress, it did not address the delayed response to the initial complaint.
This failure leads to a determination of service failure in the landlord’s complaint handling. The landlord is ordered to pay £50 compensation to the resident.
